Versioned Pod, Node, Namespace and DaemonSet lists with explicit admitted requests, init containers, Pod overhead and positive node allocatable CPU/memory
guarded: Fresh complete scoped inventory with exact cluster fingerprint, Namespace, DaemonSet, Pod and current Node identities
Versioned Pod, Node, Namespace and DaemonSet lists with explicit admitted requests, init containers, Pod overhead and positive node allocatable CPU/memory

limitations: Values describe current effective requests including init and restartable-sidecar ordering, not usage, readiness, free capacity or historical membership.
Only observed assigned nonterminal DaemonSet Pods are compared; unassigned or unresolved Pods remain evidence gaps and no missing Pod is synthesized.
Mixed admitted requests, duplicate Pods on a node, unknown lifecycle/resource accounting and missing node capacity block that DaemonSet's comparison.
Different percentages are owner-review context without a universal materiality threshold or safe per-node request target.

Desired and ready controller counts are independently retained review context with unverified generation binding; count agreement or differences do not establish desired Node membership, missing Pod placement or disruption feasibility.
No NodePool eligibility, GPU/extended-resource fit, storage, packing, replacement, removable-node or savings claim is made.
prerequisites: Confirm the DaemonSet owner and whether heterogeneous nodes need distinct resource policies using approved tooling.
risks: Current requests may protect initialization, restartable sidecars or failure scenarios; lower percentages do not authorize a reduction.
validation: Recheck exact Pod/controller/node identities and admitted requests, init ordering, Pod overhead and allocatable capacity.
Review controller desired/ready status separately from complete current owned-Pod and Node counts; unknown status does not invalidate independent observed request shares.
Review node-specific demand, startup and reliability evidence independently before any separately approved sizing experiment.
rollback: No change is proposed. Preserve exact original DaemonSet settings for rollback of any separately approved experiment.

baseline: Review observed request-share differences with the DaemonSet and platform owners; do not generate or apply node-specific sizing.
guarded: Review observed request-share differences; guarded mode does not authorize sizing, admission annotations or node changes.

manifest.baseline_summary: Identical admitted DaemonSet requests occupy different fractions of current node allocatable capacity. This is owner-review context, not a universal target, usage measurement, placement claim or savings.
manifest.guarded_summary: Identical admitted DaemonSet requests occupy different fractions of current node allocatable capacity. Guarded mode does not authorize sizing, admission annotations, placement or node removal.

manifest.title: Review CPU request
manifest.purpose: Compare observed CPU usage with the admitted request, then validate one exact upstream request candidate against policy and reliability bounds.

baseline: Complete fresh scoped Azure, Kubernetes and Prometheus receipts
Exact cluster/workload identity and declared direct or approved replica-envelope usage
Observed positive admitted CPU request and qualified P95 usage
Configured observation duration, coverage, freshness and resolution
guarded: One exact fresh per-container VPA or Kubecost candidate from a characterized source version matching current workload, request and unit
All baseline evidence, qualified P99/observed peaks, throttling and OOM history
Known compatible autoscalers and no observed OOM or workload eviction veto
Owner-reviewed window, disruption policy, environment, minimum, headroom and reduction bounds

limitations: Low CPU usage is not a safe reduction target or proof a node can be removed.
Requests are not CPU limits; a request ratio is not saturation.
Current identities cannot reconstruct missing history or deleted membership.
Replica-envelope statistics are conservative per-replica values, not workload-total percentiles.
Returned evaluation-point coverage is not raw scrape completeness.
Candidate conflicts are evaluated per exact container and resource dimension; unknown source versions remain blocked.
A current Off-mode VPA does not establish historical nonmutation; independent controller and request history remains required.
prerequisites: Confirm the metric window contains peak and business-critical periods.
Review P99 usage, throttling, startup and failover behavior.
risks: Historical usage might not represent future peaks.
Lower requests can change placement and noisy-neighbor behavior.
validation: Run VPA in Off mode and compare recommendations.
Canary an independently approved request change and verify SLOs under load.
rollback: Restore the previous CPU request of __current_cpu_request__ mCPU in source configuration through the owning delivery pipeline.
Stop promotion if SLOs, throttling, OOM or restarts regress; remeasure before proposing another change.
baseline_rollback: No numeric change is proposed; do not apply a baseline investigation.

baseline: Review observed usage, owner requirements and missing guarded evidence.
guarded: Review the validated upstream request candidate and rollback criteria before any customer-owned PR.

manifest.baseline_summary: Observed P95 CPU usage is below the configured fraction of the current admitted request. This is an investigation, not a safe reduction target; owner policy, peaks and reliability must be reviewed independently.
manifest.guarded_summary: The upstream CPU request candidate is not below the accelerator safety floor and passed the required evidence gates; validate it through a separately approved canary.

review_ratio.implication: Investigation threshold only, not a utilization target or proposal bound. Equality produces no signal; safety/owner gates cannot be overridden.

manifest.title: Investigate current placement constraints

baseline: Fresh complete scoped inventory with exact cluster, Namespace, Pod and controller UIDs
guarded: Fresh complete scoped inventory with exact cluster, Namespace, Pod and controller UIDs

limitations: Current metadata is not historical scheduling behavior, a packing simulation or proof of stranded capacity.
Projected labels cannot prove selector matches or absence. Namespace PDB candidates are not matched budgets.
Tolerations permit placement but do not require it. Soft preferences are distinct from hard constraints.
Volume bindings, CSI topology, Pod/IP slots, priority/preemption, daemon requests and availability need independent review.
prerequisites: Review the admitted Pod, matching node labels/taints, volume topology and actual PDB selectors with its owner.
risks: Relaxing affinity, topology, taints or disruption policy can violate isolation, availability or storage requirements.
validation: Correlate each observed restriction with approved pending-Pod history and scheduler capacity evidence.
Check daemon and init/sidecar overhead, Pod/IP slots, priorities, volumes and zonal failover before any packing claim.
Keep hard requirements and soft preferences separate; verify unknown fields rather than assuming absence.
rollback: No change is proposed. Any later owner-approved experiment requires a separate canary and exact configuration rollback.

baseline: Investigate current placement restrictions; do not remove nodes or relax policy from this report.
guarded: Investigate current placement restrictions; guarded mode does not authorize a scheduling change.

manifest.title: Review current optimization constraints
manifest.purpose: Identify current probe, topology-spread and voluntary-disruption evidence that needs owner review before scaling, disruption or consolidation decisions.

baseline: Fresh complete scoped inventory with exact cluster, Namespace, Pod, controller and PDB identities
Sanitized per-container probe presence, typed topology-spread details and namespace PDB availability/status evidence
Explicit current controller replica count of at least two for topology-spread findings
guarded: Fresh complete scoped inventory with exact cluster, Namespace, Pod, controller and PDB identities
Sanitized per-container probe presence, typed topology-spread details and namespace PDB availability/status evidence
Explicit current controller replica count of at least two for topology-spread findings

limitations: Unavailable PDB inventory for observed Pods produces an independent evidence gap without hiding qualified probe or topology findings.
Probe presence does not establish application health, correct timing or safe probe behavior; probe handlers and payloads are not collected.
Missing topology spread is an owner review candidate, not proof that spreading is required or that a workload is portable.
Omitted/defaulted replica counts remain unknown; topology findings are limited to explicitly replicated Deployment and StatefulSet workloads.
PDB selector matching is unknown. Zero allowed disruptions is a point-in-time voluntary-disruption constraint, not proof that a PDB is universally too strict.
Current metadata is not historical behavior, disruption feasibility, a node-removal plan or evidence of savings.
prerequisites: Ask the workload owner which startup, health, availability, failure-domain and disruption behavior the application requires.
Verify actual PDB selectors and eligible Pods with approved Kubernetes tooling before relating a budget to a workload.
risks: Adding probes without application semantics can cause restart loops or remove healthy endpoints from service.
Changing topology or disruption policy can reduce availability, violate storage constraints or increase correlated failure risk.
validation: Validate probe behavior during startup, steady state, dependency failure and graceful termination using owner-approved tests.
Validate replica placement and failure-domain behavior before any topology-policy experiment.
Recheck actual PDB selectors, desired healthy counts and disruptions allowed immediately before any separately approved voluntary disruption.
rollback: No configuration is generated or applied. Restore any separately approved probe, topology or PDB experiment through the owner's delivery system if validation regresses.

baseline: Review the observed constraints with the workload and platform owners; do not generate or apply configuration from this finding.
guarded: Review the observed constraints with the workload and platform owners; guarded mode does not authorize or generate a change.

manifest.baseline_summary: Current probe, topology or voluntary-disruption evidence may constrain scaling, disruption, consolidation or portability. The finding is an owner investigation, not a selector match, universal policy judgment or generated configuration.
manifest.guarded_summary: Current probe, topology or voluntary-disruption evidence may constrain scaling, disruption, consolidation or portability. Guarded mode does not authorize a change or generate configuration.

manifest.title: Investigate observed readiness and subsequent demand
manifest.purpose: Review a bounded sampled Pod readiness transition within one exact observed container attempt and independently qualified post-readiness measurements.

baseline: Complete aligned saved native lifecycle observations with exact cluster, Namespace, workload, Pod and container-attempt identity and original source clocks
Fresh scoped current inventory and an observed not-ready to ready transition without changed or missing attempt evidence
guarded: Complete aligned saved native lifecycle observations with exact cluster, Namespace, workload, Pod and container-attempt identity and original source clocks
Fresh scoped current inventory and an observed not-ready to ready transition without changed or missing attempt evidence

limitations: Explicitly selected saved-history pack; default analysis retains its original pack selection.
Bounds describe a sampled Pod readiness proxy, not first-ever startup, continuous history or application initialization latency.
A zero restart counter and stable sampled runtime digest do not prove historical absence of restarts between samples.
Usage requires its own exact catalog query, full aligned coverage and a separate post-readiness window inside the sampled attempt; CPU rate lookback must also follow readiness.
Missing usage does not erase independently valid readiness observations; working set is not full-memory usage and no representative-demand claim is supplied.
Saved source consistency is not authentication or actual-source compatibility certification. No target, autoscaling suitability or savings is supplied.
prerequisites: Obtain approved existing saved lifecycle evidence; do not install an observer, collect Events/logs or infer history from current status.
risks: Pod readiness may reflect probes or readiness gates rather than application initialization, and sampling can miss transitions or peaks.
validation: Review exact Pod/container identity, original receipts, sample cadence and readiness criterion before interpreting the observed bracket.
Review independent application startup, SLO, peak, failover and representative usage evidence before considering any change.
rollback: No change is proposed; preserve original settings for rollback of any separately approved experiment.

baseline: Review the observed readiness bracket and independent measurement gaps with the workload owner; do not choose a resource or replica target.
guarded: Review the observed readiness bracket; guarded mode does not authorize sizing, scale-to-zero or remediation.

manifest.baseline_summary: Saved samples bracket an observed Pod readiness transition. This is not application startup duration, proof of a first attempt or a safe resource setting.
manifest.guarded_summary: Saved samples bracket an observed Pod readiness transition. Guarded mode does not authorize resource, replica or startup-policy changes.

glossary.baseline: Qualified investigations only; no numeric resource or replica proposals.
glossary.guarded: Guarded mode is not approval. Numeric proposals require independent owner policy, complete identity-bound evidence, reliability gates and a one-dimensional canary/rollback. Configuration never enables owner opt-ins or changes a cluster.
glossary.coverage: Returned evaluation points, not proof of raw scrape completeness.
glossary.identity: Historical UIDs and exact Azure IDs; current names cannot backfill history.
glossary.unknown: Missing or unsupported evidence is not zero or proof of health.
glossary.query-only: Executable exports measure signals; they do not pass assessment gates.
glossary.provenance: Pack/query versions and digests bind replay, not source attestation.
glossary.mCPU: One thousandth of a CPU core.
glossary.MiB: 1,048,576 bytes; working set and full usage are distinct measurements.
glossary.ratio: Dimensionless fraction; not a universal utilization target.
glossary.events: Complete interval counts; missing intervals are not zero.
glossary.pods: Sampled replica counts, not availability or safe capacity by themselves.
glossary.boolean: Explicit observed state; missing observations remain unknown.

guarded_notice: Guarded mode is not approval. Numeric proposals require independent owner policy, complete identity-bound evidence, reliability gates and a one-dimensional canary/rollback. Configuration never enables owner opt-ins or changes a cluster.
